previous_clause: An endpoint MAY allow a period of approximately the Probe Timeout (PTO; see [QUIC-RECOVERY]) after promoting the next set of receive keys to be current before it creates the subsequent set of packet protection keys.
target_clause: These updated keys MAY replace the previous keys at that time.
next_clause: With the caveat that PTO is a subjective measure - that is, a peer could have a different view of the RTT - this time is expected to be long enough that any reordered packets would be declared lost by a peer even if they were acknowledged and short enough to allow a peer to initiate further key updates.

previous_clause: In this case, the Key Phase bit alone can be used to select keys.
target_clause: An endpoint MAY allow a period of approximately the Probe Timeout (PTO; see [QUIC-RECOVERY]) after receiving a packet that uses the new key generation before it creates the next set of packet protection keys.
next_clause: These updated keys MAY replace the previous keys at that time.

previous_clause: Servers SHOULD ensure that tokens sent in Retry packets are only accepted for a short time, as they are returned immediately by clients.
target_clause: Tokens that are provided in NEW_TOKEN frames ([frame-new-token]) need to be valid for longer, but SHOULD NOT be accepted multiple times.
next_clause: Servers are encouraged to allow tokens to be used only once, if possible; tokens MAY include additional information about clients to further narrow applicability or reuse.

previous_clause: A packet might be held in the OS kernel or elsewhere on the host before being processed.
target_clause: An endpoint MUST NOT include delays that it does not control when populating the Ack Delay field in an ACK frame.

previous_clause: If the PING frame is determined to be lost, a new PING frame SHOULD be generated.
target_clause: This PING frame MUST include a new Data field that is similarly difficult to guess.
next_clause: If validation of the new remote address fails, after allowing enough time for possible loss and recovery of packets carrying PING and PONG frames, the endpoint MUST terminate the connection.

previous_clause: An implementation MUST ignore the contents for any SETTINGS identifier it does not understand.
target_clause: SETTINGS frames always apply to a connection, never a single stream, and MUST only be sent on the connection control stream (Stream 3).
next_clause: If an endpoint receives an SETTINGS frame whose stream identifier field is anything other than 0x0, the endpoint MUST respond with a connection error of type HTTP_SETTINGS_ON_WRONG_STREAM.

previous_clause: This increase could result in congestion and loss.
target_clause: A sender MAY attempt to detect suppression of reports by marking occasional packets that they send with ECN-CE.
next_clause: If a packet sent with ECN-CE is not reported as having been CE marked when the packet is acknowledged, then the sender SHOULD disable ECN for that path.

previous_clause: An endpoint SHOULD treat receipt of an acknowledgment for a packet it did not send as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION, if it is able to detect the condition.
target_clause: The receiver’s delayed acknowledgment timer SHOULD NOT exceed the current RTT estimate or the value it indicates in the max_ack_delay transport parameter.
next_clause: This ensures an acknowledgment is sent at least once per RTT when packets needing acknowledgement are received.

previous_clause: It is unlikely that the client port number is the same on two different connections; validating the port is therefore unlikely to be successful.
target_clause: If the client has a token received in a NEW_TOKEN frame on a previous connection to what it believes to be the same server, it SHOULD include that value in the Token field of its Initial packet.
next_clause: Including a token might allow the server to validate the client address without an additional round trip.

previous_clause: An endpoint MAY send data to an unvalidated peer address, but it MUST protect against potential attacks as described in [address-spoofing] and [on-path-spoofing].
target_clause: An endpoint MAY skip validation of a peer address if that address has been seen recently.
next_clause: In particular, if an endpoint returns to a previously-validated path after detecting some form of spurious migration, skipping address validation and restoring loss detection and congestion state can reduce the performance impact of the attack.

previous_clause: Abrupt Shutdown: An endpoint may send a Public Reset packet at any time during the connection to abruptly terminate an active connection.
target_clause: A Public Reset packet SHOULD only be used as a final recourse.
next_clause: Commonly, a public reset is expected to be sent when a packet on an established connection is received by an endpoint that is unable decrypt the packet.

previous_clause: An endpoint MAY abandon address validation for an address that it considers to be already valid.
target_clause: That is, if successive connection migrations occur in quick succession with the final remote address being identical to the initial remote address, the endpoint MAY abandon address validation for that address.

previous_clause: A zero-length connection ID can be used when a connection ID is not needed to route to the correct endpoint.
target_clause: However, multiplexing connections on the same local IP address and port while using zero-length connection IDs will cause failures in the presence of peer connection migration, NAT rebinding, and client port reuse; and therefore MUST NOT be done unless an endpoint is certain that those protocol features are not in use.
next_clause: When an endpoint uses a non-zero-length connection ID, it needs to ensure that the peer has a supply of connection IDs from which to choose for packets sent to the endpoint.

previous_clause: The server MUST include all settings that differ from their default values.
target_clause: If a server accepts 0-RTT but then sends settings that are not compatible with the previously specified settings, this MUST be treated as a connection error of type H3_SETTINGS_ERROR.
next_clause: If a server accepts 0-RTT but then sends a SETTINGS frame that omits a setting value that the client understands (apart from reserved setting identifiers) that was previously specified to have a non-default value, this MUST be treated as a connection error of type H3_SETTINGS_ERROR.

previous_clause: If a sender has sent data up to the limit, it will be unable to send new data and is considered blocked. A sender SHOULD send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame to indicate to the receiver that it has data to write but is blocked by flow control limits.
target_clause: If a sender is blocked for a period longer than the idle timeout ([idle-timeout]), the receiver might close the connection even when the sender has data that is available for transmission. To keep the connection from closing, a sender that is flow control limited SHOULD periodically send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame when it has no ack-eliciting packets in flight.
An endpoint SHOULD abandon path validation after sending some number of PATH_CHALLENGE frames or after some time has passed.
next_clause: When setting this timer, implementations are cautioned that the new path could have a longer round-trip time than the original.

previous_clause: This also helps reduce the amplitude of amplification attacks caused by server responses toward an unverified client address; see [address-validation].
target_clause: Datagrams containing Initial packets MAY exceed 1200 bytes if the client believes that the network path and peer both support the size that it chooses.
next_clause: A server MUST discard an Initial packet that is carried in a UDP datagram with a payload that is less than the smallest allowed maximum packet size of 1200 bytes.

previous_clause: If a server isn’t currently accepting any new connections, it SHOULD send an Initial packet containing a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with error code SERVER_BUSY.
target_clause: If the packet is a 0-RTT packet, the server MAY buffer a limited number of these packets in anticipation of a late-arriving Initial Packet.
next_clause: Clients are forbidden from sending Handshake packets prior to receiving a server response, so servers SHOULD ignore any such packets.

previous_clause: Packets that are not ack-eliciting are only acknowledged when an ACK frame is sent for other reasons.
target_clause: When sending a packet for any reason, an endpoint SHOULD attempt to bundle an ACK frame if one has not been sent recently.
next_clause: Doing so helps with timely loss detection at the peer.

previous_clause: Once a connection exists to a server endpoint, this connection MAY be reused for requests with multiple different URI authority components.
target_clause: The client MAY send any requests for which the client considers the server authoritative.
next_clause: An authoritative HTTP/3 endpoint is typically discovered because the client has received an Alt-Svc record from the request's origin which nominates the endpoint as a valid HTTP Alternative Service for that origin.
